query: How do the adaptive engine and survival decay interact with HDBSCAN clusters?

recall_results.summary: M3 per-cluster Kaplan-Meier survival decay replaces fixed Ebbinghaus when sufficient data exists per cluster; the cluster IDs come from M4 HDBSCAN output.
evidence_preview: fallback to fixed Ebbinghaus on cold start

recall_results.summary: M2 counterfactual alpha optimization learns CC fusion weights per cluster from candidate replay; alpha values are stored in AdaptiveState and updated event-sourced.
HDBSCAN extracts flat clusters from a stability-scored condensed tree using EOMBST; output feeds both the M2 alpha learner and the M3 survival estimator.
STM to LTM promotion thresholds are derived from cluster-level survival curves when available; otherwise a global access_count > 5 fallback is used.
M5 Hot/Warm/Cold tiering uses a streaming t-digest quantile estimator over the HDBSCAN cluster of each memory to pick adaptive tier boundaries.

query: What landed in v0.23 and v0.24 around resummerize and ARS?

recall_results.summary: v0.23.0-rc1 introduced LLM-driven resummerize with the 7-invariant Lossless Compression Contract gating every rewrite; feature-flagged off by default via [resummerize].enabled.
Atomic apply_resummerize uses BEGIN IMMEDIATE plus a 5-way CAS (claim token, snapshot updated_at, status-live) to apply the LLM rewrite safely.
v0.24 ARS Capability A added concept living-summary refresh with L3 adaptive wiring and L4 concurrent CAS; opt-in via [ars].concept_summary_enabled.
v0.25 ARS Capability B added recall-time synthesis: optional synthesize=true on rein_recall produces a narrative over top-N results without a new MCP tool.
